scope: Read-only inspection of dataset directories, embedded image metadata, sidecar files, filename patterns and repository documentation. No dataset file, run, result or prior-phase output was modified.
hard_rules_applied: A filename component becomes a patient key only if dataset documentation explicitly defines it as one.

source_provenance.index_variable_source: df.iterrows() -> i is the pandas row index of the source parquet

candidate_grouping_keys.candidate: Identifier column in the source dataset
candidate_grouping_keys.would_group_by: a patient/study/series field shipped with the upstream data
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: src/prepare_dataset.py references only ['image', 'label'] from the source parquet (Hemg/Brain-Tumor-MRI-Dataset, file data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet). No identifier column is read, and none is written to disk.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: The conversion script consumes only the image bytes and the class label. Even if the upstream parquet carried an identifier, it was not retained in this repository's copy, so it cannot be recovered from what is on disk.

candidate_grouping_keys.candidate: DICOM / NIfTI header metadata (PatientID, StudyInstanceUID, SeriesInstanceUID)
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Files with medical-imaging extensions: none. Files carrying the DICOM 'DICM' preamble at byte 128: 0. Every image is a re-encoded consumer-format file.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: No DICOM or NIfTI file exists in this repository. The dataset is distributed as JPEG, which does not carry DICOM headers. Absence was established by magic-byte inspection of every file, not assumed from the file extension.

candidate_grouping_keys.would_group_by: acquisition timestamp, device, or a custom identifier tag
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Images carrying any EXIF tag: 0. Embedded info keys present across the corpus: ['comment', 'jfif', 'jfif_density', 'jfif_unit', 'jfif_version'].
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: No image carries EXIF. The only embedded keys are JFIF density markers, which encode pixel aspect ratio and contain no subject, device or timing information.

candidate_grouping_keys.candidate: Sidecar manifest or label file shipped with the dataset
candidate_grouping_keys.would_group_by: a mapping column from filename to patient
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Non-image files inside the dataset directories: 2 (dataset_clean/split_manifest.json, dataset_clean/split_report.json). Of these, 2 were generated by this project's own deduplication step and contain no patient field.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: The dataset ships no sidecar metadata. The only non-image files are artifacts this project created, whose schema is class and split membership, not subject identity.

candidate_grouping_keys.candidate: Numeric suffix of internal filenames, e.g. glioma_00243.jpg
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Filename construction is f"{args.out_dir}/{split}/{cls}/{cls}_{i:05d}.jpg", quality=95, iterating df.iterrows() -> i is the pandas row index of the source parquet. The number is therefore the row position in the source parquet.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: The index is an export counter assigned by this repository's own conversion script. It encodes position in a dataframe, not a subject. Treating adjacent indices as one patient would fabricate groupings.

candidate_grouping_keys.would_group_by: the 'Tr-xx' prefix or the trailing Roboflow hash
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Distinct filename shapes in the external set: ['Tr-gl_<N>_jpg.rf.<HEX>', 'Tr-pi_<N>_jpg.rf.<HEX>', 'Tr-no_<N>_jpg.rf.<HEX>', 'm<N>-<N>-_jpg.rf.<HEX>']. The '.rf.<hex>' component is a Roboflow export content hash; the 'Tr-' prefix denotes the upstream archive's own train folder.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: No dataset documentation available here defines either component as a patient or study identifier. The Roboflow hash is a per-image content digest, so it is unique per image and groups nothing. Promoting an undocumented prefix to a patient key is explicitly out of bounds.

candidate_grouping_keys.would_group_by: images within a dHash Hamming radius
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Not evaluated. Excluded before inspection by the Phase 2 rules.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: Visual similarity is not identity. Two slices from one study may be near-duplicates, and so may scans of two unrelated subjects with similar anatomy at a similar slice level. Using similarity clusters as a patient key would assume the conclusion the audit exists to test.

candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Not evaluated. Excluded before inspection by the Phase 2 rules.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: Contiguity reflects export ordering. See C5: the ordering here is parquet row order, which has no documented relationship to acquisition or subject.

candidate_grouping_keys.would_group_by: the folder an image sits in
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: Directory levels observed are split (Training/Testing) and diagnostic class (glioma, meningioma, notumor, pituitary). No subject-level directory exists.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: The hierarchy encodes split and class only. It carries no subject level.

candidate_grouping_keys.candidate: A documented naming convention from the dataset source
candidate_grouping_keys.evidence: 46 repository files inspected for identifier definitions; 19 lines mention identifier-like terms, none of which defines a patient, study or series key for these filenames.
candidate_grouping_keys.reason: No documentation in this repository, and none shipped with the data, defines a patient/study identifier or a filename convention that encodes one.

conclusion: Patient-level independence cannot be verified from the available dataset metadata.
grouped_cross_validation_note: No GroupKFold, grouped split or patient-level result was computed or fabricated. With no defensible key, any such number would be fiction.
